video_title: 🇻🇪 Carl Herrera ABRE su corazón y manda un GRAN mensaje | E4 T1 Voces NBA

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his disastrous rookie season in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: My first year as a rookie was disastrous. I was hit from all sides.
quotes.quote: My first year as a rookie was disastrous. I was hit from all sides. I said, this is not for me.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Mi primer año de rookie desastroso. Me pegaron por todos lados. Yo decía, esto como que no es para mí.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the lack of basketball infrastructure in Venezuela
quotes.excerpt: Venezuela was not a factor in basketball. It was baseball, then football, then volleyball, then basketball.
quotes.quote: Venezuela was not a factor in basketball. It was baseball, then football, then volleyball, then basketball. Basketball was in fourth place. As a good Venezuelan, I started playing baseball first in school, then I started to try a little bit of volleyball, and then it was how the basketball part started for me.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Venezuela no es o no era un factor en lo que es la parte de baloncesto. Más que todo era el béisbol, después era el fútbol y después venía el voleibol y después el baloncesto. El baloncesto estaba de cuarto. Yo como todo buen venezolano, comencé a jugar béisbol primero en la escuela y luego empecé a probar un poquito con el voleibol y después vino el baloncesto.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the difficulty of finding basketball shoes in Venezuela
quotes.excerpt: I had only one pair of sneakers. With that, I trained, went to school, and played.
quotes.quote: I had only one pair of sneakers. With that, I trained, went to school, and played. So, it was for everything. And getting sneakers of that size in Venezuela was very, very difficult.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Tenía una sola. Con esa iba entrenaba, iba al colegio, jugaba. Así que bueno, los sábados para todo y conseguir zapatillas de ese tamaño en Venezuela era muy, muy difícil.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his family's financial struggles in Venezuela
quotes.excerpt: We never had our own house. We had to invade a house.
quotes.quote: In Caracas, we moved a lot. My father was looking for a scenario, we never had our own house. We had to invade a house. I'm talking about the 80s when Venezuela was a potential, there were many immigrants, the currency was 4.30 to the dollar, but we were having a very bad time, very bad.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: En Caracas nos mudábamos mucho. Mi padre buscando un escenario, nunca tuvimos una casa propia. Tuvimos que invadir una casa. Te estoy hablando de los 80 cuando Venezuela era un potencial, había muchos inmigrantes, la moneda estaba 4.30 al dólar, pero nosotros la estábamos pasando muy mal, muy mal.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on receiving a scholarship to play in the US
quotes.excerpt: Gabriel called me after the game and said, I have a surprise. I have an I-20.
quotes.quote: Gabriel called me after the game and said, I have a surprise. I have an I-20, I have a scholarship for you to go to the United States. I sat down and I really didn't believe it. I said, Gabriel, you are lying to me. He said, no, I have it. He showed it to me and I cried, I hugged him, I thanked him because it was what I wanted, the opportunity to go to the United States to study, to get my family ahead.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Me llamó después del partido y me dijo, Carl, te tengo una sorpresa. Te tengo una I-20, te tengo una beca para que te vayas a Estados Unidos. Yo me senté y de verdad que no me lo creía. Yo le dije, Gabriel, tú me estás mintiendo. Me dice, no, me la tengo. Me la enseñó y lloré, lo abracé, le agradecí porque era lo que yo, lo que yo anhelaba, la oportunidad de Estados Unidos, estudiar, sacar a mi familia adelante.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the responsibility he felt for his family
quotes.excerpt: My father had started having Parkinson's problems. My mother had been operated on for a brain tumor.
quotes.quote: My father had started having Parkinson's problems. My mother had been operated on for a brain tumor while I was playing in the Pan American games. So, the future of my brother, the future of my son, and my future were there. I had to go.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Mi padre ya había comenzado con problemas de Parkinson. Mi mamá la habían operado de un tumor en el cerebro mientras yo estaba jugando los Panamericanos. O sea que el futuro de mi hermano, el futuro de mi hijo y el futuro mío estaban ahí. Me tenía que ir.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his coach's advice regarding his future
quotes.excerpt: I told the coach I was leaving. He said, you are in Venezuela, what do you have there?
quotes.quote: I told the coach I was leaving. He said, you are in Venezuela, what do you have there? Your family, it's missing less for you to graduate and give your family a better life. You want to leave? My first year as a rookie was disastrous. I was hit from all sides. I said, this is not for me.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Le dije que me iba. Y me dijo, ¿qué tienes en Venezuela tú, tu familia? Te falta menos para graduarte y darle a tu familia una mejor vida. ¿Te quieres ir? Mi primer año de rookie desastroso. Me pegaron por todos lados. Yo decía, esto como que no es para mí.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his coach's advice to finish his degree
quotes.excerpt: You have less time left to graduate, go to a first-division university, be taken into account.
quotes.quote: You have less time left to graduate, go to a first-division university, be taken into account. And if you don't sign with the NBA, you can go play in Europe and give your family a better life. You are going to graduate. You want to leave?
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Te falta menos para graduarte, ir a una universidad de primera división, te tomen en cuenta. Y si no firmas con la NBA, te puedes ir a jugar en Europa y darle a tu familia una mejor vida. Te vas a graduar. ¿Te quieres ir?

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the importance of staying grounded
quotes.excerpt: My mother was a very humble woman, very centered, with her feet firmly on the ground.
quotes.quote: My mother was a very humble woman, very centered, with her feet firmly on the ground. My father supported me a lot in that. And she told me, and my father told me, that the only way, although they told me what they told me, informing like a cloud of expectations around me, that I could arrive, that I was a god, that this, the only way to do it was by working. And I focused on that.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Mi mamá era una mujer muy humilde, muy, muy centrada, con sus pies bien puestos en la tierra. Sí, sí, centrada. Mi padre la apoyaba mucho en eso. Y ella me decía y mi padre me decía, que la única forma, aunque me dijeran lo que me dijeran, informaran como una nube de expectativas a mi alrededor, de que yo podía llegar, de que yo era un dios, de que esto, la única forma de hacerlo era trabajando. Y yo me enfoqué en eso.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his success at the junior college level
quotes.excerpt: The second year, Larry Johnson and I were the best junior college players, considered one and two.
quotes.quote: The second year, Larry Johnson and I were the best junior college players, considered one and two, coming out of junior college. We had many university offers. In fact, I was going to go to UNLV with him, but after four visits, I decided to go to the University of Houston.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Luego el segundo año, Larry Johnson y yo fuimos los mejores jugadores de Junior College, considerado uno y dos, saliendo de Junior College. Tuvimos muchas ofertas de universidad. De hecho, yo iba a ir a UNLV con él, pero después de cuatro visitas, decidí ir para la Universidad de Houston.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his father's heart condition
quotes.excerpt: My father had a heart problem. That hit me very hard.
quotes.quote: My father had a heart problem. That hit me very hard. And I was very hurried by the monetary situation to be able to help them. And I put my name in the draft at that moment.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Mi padre tuvo un problema cardíaco. Eso me pegó muchísimo. Y estaba como que muy apurado por la situación monetaria para poderlos ayudar. Y puse mi nombre en el draft en ese momento.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on how he got signed by Real Madrid
quotes.excerpt: We sent some videos to Europe, Real Madrid, Barcelona, and Real Madrid was interested.
quotes.quote: We sent some videos to Europe, Real Madrid, Barcelona, and Real Madrid was interested. There was Wayne Brabender, I don't know if you've heard of him. A reference of Real Madrid, he was American, but he naturalized Spanish. And when Wayne sees the videos, he starts talking to my agent. He went to Venezuela to see me play with the Portuguese team. That year we were champion, that was in 90. And he was in one of the games where I hit a triple to win a game, to win that game. And we won the championship in seven games.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Mandamos unos videos a Europa, Real Madrid, Barcelona y Real Madrid se interesó. Estaba Wayne Brabender, yo no sé si lo has escuchado. Un referente del Real Madrid, él era americano, pero se naturalizó español. Y cuando Wayne ve los videos, empieza a hablar con mi agente. Él fue a Venezuela a verme jugar con el equipo Portuguesa. Ese año quedamos campeón, fue en el 90. Y él estuvo en uno de los partidos donde yo metí un triple para ganar un partido, para ganar ese partido. Y ganamos el campeonato en siete juegos.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on his first big contract
quotes.excerpt: The first thing I did was buy a house, give my parents a better situation.
quotes.quote: The first thing I did was buy a house, give my parents a better situation. My life took a turn and I didn't believe it. The amount of money I was earning, the tension that Real Madrid gave me, I didn't know that Real Madrid was an organization like the one it is.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Lo primero que hice fue comprar una casa, darle a mis padres una mejor situación. Mi vida dio un vuelco y no me lo creía. La cantidad de dinero que estaba ganando, la tensión que me daba el Real Madrid, yo no sabía que el Real Madrid era una organización como la que es.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on why he didn't want to play in the NBA initially
quotes.excerpt: I have a lot of respect, after having seen Magic, after having seen Barkley, and I said, I'm going.
quotes.quote: I have a lot of respect, after having seen Magic, after having seen Barkley, and I said, I'm going there, I play a year, then I don't play anymore. No, I'm staying in Europe. You have fear of the NBA? No, I don't have fear, I have a lot of respect, after having seen Magic, after having seen Barkley, and I said, I'm going there, I play a year, then I don't play anymore. No, I'm staying in Europe.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Le tengo miedo a la NBA? No, no le tengo miedo, le tengo mucho respeto, después de haber visto a Magic, después de haber visto a Barkley, y yo decía, voy allá, juego un año, después no juego más. No, me quedo en Europa.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the physical toll of his rookie season
quotes.excerpt: My weight was not for playing four, I played three. I hit my back, my ankles.
quotes.quote: My weight was not for playing four, I played three. I hit my back, my ankles, and well, I said, this is not for me. Already after that year, with the national team, we had the opportunity to win the first South American in 90-91 in Venezuela. We beat Brazil by 15 points. Everything, NBC, all the American television stations had the final, Brazil and the Dream Team of the United States. When we beat Brazil, we went to the final against the United States.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Mi peso no era para jugar cuatro, yo jugaba tres. Me pegaron la espalda, los tobillos y bueno, yo decía, esto como que no es para mí. Ya después de ese año, con la selección nacional, tuvimos la oportunidad de ganar el primer Sudamericano en el 90-91 en Venezuela. Le ganamos a Brasil por 15 puntos. Todo, NBC, todas las televisoras americanas tenían la final, Brasil y el Dream Team de Estados Unidos. Cuando le ganamos a Brasil, fuimos a la final contra Estados Unidos.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the transition to a role player
quotes.excerpt: It was difficult because being a reference in Venezuela, I was a starter, I played 40 minutes.
quotes.quote: It was difficult because being a reference in Venezuela, I was a starter, I played 40 minutes. In the national team, I played 40 minutes. In Real Madrid, I played 40 minutes. When I get to the NBA, I pretended to play position three, not to say that I wanted to play 40 minutes or 44, but yes, to have 30 and something minutes, and it gave me a shock. I had players potentially like me, or better than me, and Rudy, in a moment when I saw my face, I was annoyed, I was uncomfortable, Rudy calls me and takes me to an office.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Para mí fue difícil, porque ser un referente en Venezuela, yo era abridor, jugaba 40 minutos. En la selección jugaba 40 minutos. En el Real Madrid jugaba 40 minutos. Cuando yo llego a la NBA, yo pretendía jugar de puesto tres, no te voy a decir que quería jugar 40 minutos o 44, pero sí, tener 30 y algo de minutos y me dio un choque. Tenía jugadores potentemente como yo, o mejores que yo, y Rudy, en un momento cuando me vio la cara, me vio molesto, me vio incómodo, Rudy me llama y me lleva a una oficina.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the team structure Rudy Tomjanovich built
quotes.excerpt: He explained the structure of the team he wanted to build, and the players one by one.
quotes.quote: He explained the structure of the team he wanted to build, and the players one by one, from one to six. He talked to me about Kenny, he talked to me about Maxwell, he talked to me about Robert, Otis Thorpe, and obviously the star number 34, Hakeem, who is the axis of the team. He told me, after this fifth player, I don't have a sixth player like you, who can mark outside the three, who is fast, who is a perimeter defender, who at the same time can defend an internal one.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Me explica la estructura del equipo que él quería construir y los jugadores uno por uno, del uno al seis. Me habló de Kenny, me habló de Maxwell, me habló de Robert, Otis Thorpe y obviamente la estrella número 34, Hakeem, que es el eje del equipo. Me decía, después de este quinto jugador, yo no tengo un sexto jugador como tú, que pueda marcar afuera a los tres, que sea rápido, que sea un defensor perimetral, que a la vez pueda defender a un interno.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the difficulty of managing egos in the NBA
quotes.excerpt: Twelve egos is very difficult to keep together, convincing them that we come to train.
quotes.quote: Twelve egos is very difficult to keep together, convincing them that we come to train, to work for a purpose. And it doesn't matter what you earn, it doesn't matter where you come from, it doesn't matter what color you are, you have to sell that. And I said, okay, let me try, but I said, but why me? He said, Carl, because none of the other players do what you do.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Doce egos es muy difícil mantenerlos juntos, convencerlos de que venimos a entrenar, a trabajar para un propósito. Y no importa lo que ganes, no importa de dónde vengas, no importa el color que seas, tú tienes que venderle eso. Y yo dije, okay, déjame probar, pero yo dije, ¿pero por qué yo? Me dice, Carl, porque ninguno de los demás jugadores hace lo que tú haces.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on the 1994 championship run
quotes.excerpt: The second year, Larry Johnson and I were the best junior college players. We won the championship.
quotes.quote: The second year, Larry Johnson and I were the best junior college players, considered one and two. We won the championship in seven games. Wayne Brabender was American, but he naturalized Spanish. And when Wayne sees the videos, he starts talking to my agent. He went to Venezuela to see me play with the Portuguese team. That year we were champion, that was in 90. And he was in one of the games where I hit a triple to win a game, to win that game. And we won the championship in seven games.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Luego el segundo año, Larry Johnson y yo fuimos los mejores jugadores de Junior College, considerado uno y dos. Ganamos el campeonato en siete juegos. Wayne Brabender, él era americano, pero se naturalizó español. Y cuando Wayne ve los videos, empieza a hablar con mi agente. Él fue a Venezuela a verme jugar con el equipo Portuguesa. Ese año quedamos campeón, fue en el 90. Y él estuvo en uno de los partidos donde yo metí un triple para ganar un partido, para ganar ese partido. Y ganamos el campeonato en siete juegos.

quotes.speaker: Carl Herrera
quotes.summary_phrase: Carl Herrera on helping his home country of Venezuela
quotes.excerpt: I called him to ask for a favor. In my networks, I have the Messi Chef.
quotes.quote: I called him to ask for a favor. In my networks, I have the Messi Chef and all that, doing some things to raise money for food. And I asked him for the favor and he helped me, he supported me.
quotes.verbatim_original_language: Lo llamé para pedirle un favor. En mis redes tengo lo de Messi Chef y todo eso, haciendo unas cosas para recaudar dinero para comida. Y le pedí el favor y me ayudó, me apoyó.
